### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via EngineAggregateOptionsSchema (symbol, a top-level const), EngineQueryOptionsSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f13ee81541ac1f6cbc2f5b5f2aca04e24ccc260` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ec4fff953a3f513b80e830f1b92deb5206b36100` — the merge of head `53d7eec3a696cc6f1ef435d1250b025c6031df0a` into base `9f13ee81541ac1f6cbc2f5b5f2aca04e24ccc260`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ec4fff953a3f513b80e830f1b92deb5206b36100 && git checkout ec4fff953a3f513b80e830f1b92deb5206b36100
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9f13ee81541ac1f6cbc2f5b5f2aca04e24ccc260 53d7eec3a696cc6f1ef435d1250b025c6031df0a && git checkout -B drift-repro 9f13ee81541ac1f6cbc2f5b5f2aca04e24ccc260 && git merge --no-ff 53d7eec3a696cc6f1ef435d1250b025c6031df0a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f13ee81541ac1f6cbc2f5b5f2aca04e24ccc260
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9f13ee81541ac1f6cbc2f5b5f2aca04e24ccc260` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c4560f09a4242db57b0c9bf7baf267fe4ecfa4df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts + packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.test.ts (narrowing-face floor), .changeset/28059-engine-search-fields-names-a-field.md and content/docs/references/data/data-engine.mdx (prose faces, read for ②), and the cited code read on `main` at `10fc9bf1`: packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts (`QuerySchema.searchFields` L557, `FullTextSearchSchema.fields` L455), packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts (`resolveSearchFields` L263), packages/spec/src/data/hook-api.ts (`HookCountQuery` L155), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`refuseSearchOverrideNamingNoField` L754, called L13437-13438), packages/objectql/src/empty-projection-door.ts L57, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts L2734, packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts L373, packages/objectql/src/engine-empty-search-fields-refusal.test.ts, .changeset/27484-blank-search-fields-refused.md, .changeset/27683-search-fields-names-a-field.md, .changeset/27732-engine-empty-search-fields.md, content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx L112.

Inputs: card #28059 body and its four comments (triage 6522171038, claim 6523197991, the domain:server note 6523729127, the os-dev-report 6525105567); PR #28154 body, five-file list, and the three-dot diff against `main` (merge base `d6c0a75f`, 5 files, +78/-19); the 50 check-runs on `c4560f09`. Author `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note is owed.

Gate verdicts on the head: every one of the 50 check-runs is `completed`; 36 `success`, 14 `skipped` (opt-in harnesses, matrix placeholders, the schedule gate), 0 `failure`, the newest run of each name read; last completion 2026-10-30T14:43Z. Named: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Test Core (1/8 to 8/8 and the aggregate), Spec property liveness, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards: all `success`. The Docs Drift Check advisory (6525103141) names content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx; its L112 declares `searchFields?: string[]` with no claim about an empty list, so nothing there is falsified.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, and whether it is right:

1. `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.searchFields` (data-engine.zod.ts L193-194): `z.array(z.string()).optional()` becomes `searchFieldsArray().optional()`, i.e. `z.array(z.string()).min(1, SEARCH_FIELDS_NAMES_NO_FIELD)`. `[]` is refused at path `['searchFields']` with the shared sentence; `['name']`, `['name','email']`, `['']` and an absent key are kept. **Right.** It is the arm `QuerySchema.searchFields` and `FullTextSearchSchema.fields` already use, so one rule, no second `.min(1)`.
2. `EngineAggregateOptionsSchema.searchFields` (L519-520) and `EngineCountOptionsSchema.searchFields` (L566-567): the same change. **Right**, and it removes the contradiction the card names: on each of these three schemas `search: { query, fields: [] }` was already refused (the union reuses `FullTextSearchSchema`) while `searchFields: []` was admitted.
3. Published description and JSON Schema: the three members gain a `.describe()` ending in `SEARCH_FIELDS_ACCEPT_SET`, so codegen and the reference docs state the rule (`minItems: 1` plus the sentence). The regenerated content/docs/references/data/data-engine.mdx rows (L489, L574, L700) carry exactly that text. **Right.** The six-member "declarations state the accept set they enforce" test now covers all six published declarations of the override.
4. TypeScript surface: `EngineQueryOptions`/`Parsed`, `EngineAggregateOptions`/`Parsed`, `EngineCountOptions`/`Parsed` (L1388-1407) and `HookCountQuery = Omit of EngineCountOptions` (hook-api.ts L155) stay `searchFields?: string[]`; `.min(1)` does not move the inferred type. **Right**; `check:api-surface` was not stale and Type Check · workspace is green.
5. Untouched neighbours: `QueryTransportParamsSchema.$searchFields` (L975), `QuerySchema.searchFields`, `FullTextSearchSchema.fields`, the `$searchFields` to `searchFields` lowering (L794, L1130), and the legacy `DataEngine*OptionsSchema`, which declare no `searchFields` at all. A grep of `packages/spec/src` outside tests shows the six declarations above and no seventh. **Right**: the diff's claim "no published declaration of the override admits `[]`" holds on this tree.
6. Runtime reach of the narrowing: no in-repo code parses an engine option bag with these three schemas. The readers are key-set or message readers only: objectql `empty-projection-door.ts` L57 (`shape.fields.safeParse([])`), runtime `action-execution.ts` L2734 (`Object.keys(shape)`), spec `ui/action-params.zod.ts` L373 (legal key set), objectql `ENGINE_COUNT_OPTION_KEYS`. Key set unchanged, so none moves. The diff therefore changes the declared face (JSON Schema, docs, generated clients) and nothing at runtime. **Right**, and the PR body says so.
7. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the PR body and the changeset: nothing newly admitted, `[]` refused; engine option bags are not a metadata author's surface. **Right.**
8. The narrowing takes no working capability away at any consumer: the Data API doors refuse `[]` since #27484 (`assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable`), and the in-process engine refuses it since `6a648ac2` (#28108, on `main` 2026-10-30T13:29Z: `refuseSearchOverrideNamingNoField`, engine.ts L754, called before any driver read at L13437-13438, 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, words read off `FullTextSearchSchema.shape.fields`). The declaration catches up to two refusals that already exist on `main`. **Right.**
9. Test face (floor path): the #27683 stage-boundary pin ("still admits an empty list") is flipped to refusal cases (path, message, same answer as `search.fields: []`, kept lists, absent key), one per schema. **Right**; the dev's ablation on `fca20448` reports exactly the 6 new cases red with the arm reverted, and Test Core is green on the head.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28059-engine-search-fields-names-a-field.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, title `fix(spec)!`, BREAKING banner, both declaration lines line-initial (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`), exactly one `adr-0087:` marker with the category `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which is one of ADR-0087's seven categories (docs/adr/0087 L750) and whose one mechanical check (no FROM/TO prescription in the body) the body meets. The level follows AGENTS.md: a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition. Check Changeset and Lint · repo & tooling gates are green. **Level and declarations match what the diff publishes.**
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is the right arm: the accept set of three published declarations shrinks by `[]`; nothing widens; no key added, removed or renamed.
- Prose accuracy of the changeset against `main` at `10fc9bf1` (lane seat's face; named here because the "Unchanged" bullet ships in CHANGELOG):
  - **S1 (should-fix).** The "Unchanged" bullet says the in-process engine "still read[s] an empty `searchFields` as absent (the default search set) until the engine itself refuses it; the declaration is now no wider than that coming refusal". That was true of the PR's merge base `d6c0a75f` but is false on `main`: `6a648ac2` (#28108) landed at 2026-10-30T13:29Z, before this PR was opened (2026-10-30T14:21Z), and its changeset `27732-engine-empty-search-fields.md` ships in the same release. The engine refuses `searchFields: []` and `search.fields: []` 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` before any driver read, in the declaration's own words. The bullet should say the engine refuses it too (#27732), so the declaration and the engine now agree, and drop "coming refusal". The PR body's "Engine behaviour at this head" paragraph and "The engine refusal is #27732 (in flight)" are stale the same way (the body does not ship; fix for the record's reader). The "merge brought 9 commits" sentence counts the dev's local `origin/main`, not the branch GitHub merges into.
  - **S2 (should-fix).** The "Supersedes" note names only the #27683 entry's bullet. The #27484 entry's "Not yet narrowed" bullet also names `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.searchFields` as still admitting `''` and `[]`, and the #27683 entry's supersede deliberately left that one declaration standing ("other than `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.searchFields`"). This changeset is the one that closes it; name it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (os-dev-report): the claim comment writes `Clause-②: no`; order and triage write `no (narrowing)`; the PR body and changeset carry `no (narrowing)`. **Answered**: the claim line does not ship, the two carriers that do are right.
- Dev deviation 2: the 104-command gate sweep ran on `d38c42e6`, before the merge commit; the merge `c4560f09` brought no `packages/spec` change. **Answered by the head's check-runs**: all green on `c4560f09`.
- Dev deviation 3: `test:repo` not run locally. **Answered**: Test Core (8 shards and aggregate) green on the head.
- `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. None to escalate.
- domain:server note 6523729127 (stale sentence in search-fields-names-a-field.ts L29-32, "the in-process engine still reads an empty override as absent"): **taken in this PR**, the sentence is rewritten; nothing left for seat 1 to file.
- Branch: `claude/project-thread-vyenav` instead of `claude/issue-28059-slug`, declared in the claim (platform-assigned thread branch); `Implemented-by:` below uses it.
- Head ancestry: the merge base `d6c0a75f` predates `6a648ac2`; the PR is `mergeable: clean`; of the `main` commits since the base, none touches this PR's five paths (`6a648ac2` touches objectql and protocol docs; `2695de71`/`146115a9` touch other spec files), so the regenerated `data-engine.mdx` and the test file land without textual or regeneration conflict. The only effect of the gap is S1 above.
- Draft PR, `auto_merge: null`: nothing armed, nothing to disarm.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts** — judged against the ruling (card #28059 and triage 6522171038: "the engine-side `searchFields` declarations take the same declared accept set as `FullTextSearchSchema.fields`, so the declaration never admits what the engine refuses") and its first consumers (the published JSON Schema and reference docs; the engine's refusal in objectql `engine.ts`).

- Holds against the ruling: the three declarations call `searchFieldsArray()` from `./search-fields-names-a-field` (already imported at L9 for `$searchFields`), so they are the same arm, not a copy; the sentence is `SEARCH_FIELDS_NAMES_NO_FIELD`, read off the same constant the engine (engine.ts L760, via `FullTextSearchSchema.shape.fields`) and the door declarations use. The declaration and the in-process refusal now agree in accept set and in words.
- Break attempts, none succeeds: (a) `search: { query: 'x', fields: [] }` on an engine schema goes through `z.union([z.string(), FullTextSearchSchema])`; the array branch fails dirty (`too_small`), so zod reports the inner message, not `invalid_union` — the "answers `[]` as its structured `search.fields` does" test pins it per schema and is green. (b) `.optional().describe(...)` ordering matches `QuerySchema.searchFields` L557-558 on `main`, and `.shape.searchFields.description` is pinned by the six-member test. (c) A blank member `['']` is admitted, as the shared arm admits it everywhere else; the door refuses it as an unknown field and the engine intersects it away; the changeset declares it. (d) `null`: refused before and after (`.optional()` without `.nullable()`), unchanged by this diff. Observation, no fix owed here: the engine on `main` reads `searchFields: null` as a withdrawal (#27732 "Unchanged"), so on `null` the declaration is narrower than the engine; pre-existing, not this card's.
- Design is the minimal correct one: no new rule, no new module, the three sites and the docblocks only. **No finding.**

**packages/spec/src/data/search-fields-names-a-field.ts** — docblock only; the exported constants and factories are byte-identical. Judged against the tree: the new sentence "no published declaration of the override admits `[]`" is true at this head (six declarations, all on the arm; the grep in ①.5). The sentence the domain:server note flagged is gone.

- **S3 (should-fix, minor).** L24-26 still describe `./data-engine.zod.ts` as reading this module for "the transport spelling `$searchFields`" alone; after this diff it reads the arm for four declarations. One parenthetical; the paragraph is otherwise right.

**Narrowing face as a whole** (every non-prose path of the diff, the test file included): the narrowing takes no declared capability away at a consumer — both refusals it declares already exist on `main` (door since #27484, engine since `6a648ac2`) — and it makes the spec's own refusal real at the one place that still contradicted it. The test file pins refusal, path, message, parity with `search.fields`, kept lists and the absent key for each schema.

No must-fix. Should-fix: S1, S2 (changeset prose), S3 (one docblock parenthetical).
